public_rationale: By May 2024, documented campaigns were distributing generated deceptive material across major social platforms and websites. This satisfies the stated occurrence rule under the ordinary mechanism-based reading. The reports do not support a stronger claim that such content dominated platforms or persuaded large audiences; both providers describe limited reach or successful disruption.
limitations: Support depends on reading the comparison as a shared mechanism, not equal prevalence.
The main findings come from providers investigating abuse of their own services.
The campaigns mixed generated material with human activity.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Social media platforms will be polluted by automated misinformation much as the internet as a whole will be.

statement.excerpt: Social media companies better watch out, too; they will be polluted in much the same way as the internet as a whole.
statement.document_title: Automatic Disinformation Threatens Democracy— and It’s Here

from_speaker: in much the same way as the internet as a whole
our_interpretation: Pollution means repeated distribution of automatically generated deceptive material through coordinated influence campaigns on major social platforms.
Much the same way refers to the mechanism shared with websites: generated material, fabricated identities, and coordinated publication.
The statement supplies no numerical prevalence threshold, requirement of persuasive success, or deadline.
Human-directed campaigns using generated content qualify; fully autonomous operation is not required by this sentence.
criteria.support_condition: Verified post-publication investigations document repeated campaigns distributing generated deceptive material across major social platforms and websites.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The documented cases are shown not to involve generated deceptive material or actual distribution. A finite period without detected campaigns cannot by itself falsify this undated forecast.

evidence.locator: Attacker trends, Mixing old and new
evidence.explanation: The report documents multiple covert campaigns using generated material on Telegram, X, Facebook, Instagram, and websites, including Doppelganger and Zero Zeno. These establish repeated distribution through the mechanism described, while the report also says AI had not meaningfully increased audience reach.

The case study describes generated articles and comments distributed on Facebook, Instagram, X, and websites posing as activist groups, with fabricated personas and engagement. Its original May 2024 report is linked from the May 30 announcement; the page's May 1 label is not treated as its publication date.

Meta independently reports likely generated comments in an Israel-based deceptive network linking to its websites. Its findings caution against interpreting contamination as successful persuasion or overwhelming platform defenses.

conclusive_event.meets_rule: The investigation documents multiple post-publication campaigns actually distributing generated deceptive material across major social platforms and websites.
